verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing is on by default. When a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, the thread that ran the COMMIT also runs
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: checkpoint runs when WAL 'reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages' (cached text L183, L333)

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP
verdicts.evidence: changes.html under '2025-11-04 (3.51.0)': 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug was a data race ... present from SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09) ... 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and 3.53.0 (2026-04-09) fix it
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later'; changes.html dates 3.53.0 2026-04-09

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton lost writes on 3.51.2 within about 4 seconds using three connections on two threads, plain PASSIVE PRAGMA wal_checkpoint calls and a 1 GB mmap_size
verdicts.evidence: Eaton: 'two threads and three database connections', mmap_size=1073741824, walrace-present (3510200) runs real 0m4.286s/0m3.454s; 3.53.0 build stops lost writes

verdicts.claim: Antithesis caught it on 3.51.2 in 15 minutes with a concurrent write-and-checkpoint workload, and 3.51.3 ran clean
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins' ... '3.51.3 comes back clean.'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale took manual control of checkpointing ... backups detected repeated corruption starting in August 2025, and the joint investigation took about six months
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption, repeatedly'; 'we take manual control of the checkpoint process'; 'WAL-Reset took six months of hunting'

verdicts.claim: SQLite says rollback-journal modes are likely faster for transactions larger than about 100 MB
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'For transactions larger than about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely be faster.'

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_setlk_timeout() (added in 3.50.0) with the SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT flag makes the new connection wait instead
verdicts.evidence: changes.html 2025-05-29 (3.50.0): 'Add the sqlite3_setlk_timeout() interface'; setlk_timeout page documents SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT

verdicts.claim: The wal-index keeps five read marks; a reader holding WAL_READ_LOCK(N) limits backfill to the first read-mark[N] frames
verdicts.evidence: walformat.html: 'Five "read marks"' at offsets 100..119; WAL_READ_LOCK(0..4) map to read-mark[0..4]

verdicts.claim: The fix adds one check: the checkpointer compares the live WAL header salt with the copy it took at checkpoint start and skips the backfill
verdicts.evidence: Canonical: 'A single extra check is enough ... checking that a reset of the WAL did not occur since we started the checkpoint'; model: 'Salt changed, we skip the checkpoint.'
